s05.reading.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFee: Listen for the first sound: /h/at. Try again!
s05.reading.quiz.01.title: Build the Word: _at
s05.reading.quiz.02.questions.0.retryFee: Look for the short word. Try again!
s05.reading.quiz.02.title: Find the Sight Word
s05.reading.quiz.03.questions.0.prompt: Blend it: s-u-n. What's the word?
s05.reading.quiz.03.title: Blend to Read
s05.reading.quiz.04.parentNote: Say each sound slowly, then speed up.
s05.reading.quiz.04.questions.0.retryFee: Listen to the middle sound again. Try again!
s05.reading.quiz.04.questions.1.retryFee: That one has /a/ in the middle. Try again!
s05.reading.quiz.04.title: Blend It
s05.reading.story.01.pages.0.narration: A cat sat on a mat. Tap to read along.
s05.reading.story.01.pages.1.narration: The cat put on a hat. What a fat cat!
s05.reading.story.01.pages.2.narration: The cat ran with the hat. The end!
s05.reading.story.01.parentNote: Read it twice — let your child fill in the rhyming words.
s05.reading.story.01.title: The Cat and the Hat
s05.reading.story.02.pages.0.narration: The word sat on the page and would not come.
s05.reading.story.02.pages.2.narration: Bed. It was bed all along. I read it myself.
s05.reading.story.02.parentNote: Let them sound out one real word from a book.
s05.reading.story.02.title: The Word I Could Not Read
s05.science.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: Is a dog living or non-living?
s05.science.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: A rock does not grow or eat, so it is…
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.0.feedback: Living! A dog grows, eats, and breathes.
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: Is a dog living or non-living?
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.1.feedback: Non-living. A rock does not grow or eat.
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.1.narration: Is a rock living or non-living?
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.2.feedback: Living! It grows and drinks, even without moving.
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.2.narration: Is a tree living or non-living? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.3.feedback: No. Moving is not enough — it must grow and eat.
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.3.narration: A toy dog moves and makes noise. Living? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.4.feedback: Food, water and air. All three, always.
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.4.narration: What do all living things need? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.5.feedback: Now you have a test you can use on anything.
s05.science.lesson.01.steps.5.narration: Living things grow, eat and breathe.
s05.science.lesson.01.title: Living vs. Non-Living
s05.science.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: In which season do flowers bloom?
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: Flowers bloom in spring. Tap spring.
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: Tap hot summer, then leafy fall, then snowy winter.
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.2.feedback: Fall. The seasons always go in the same order.
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: Which season comes after summer? Tap it.
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.3.feedback: Winter. Weather changes what we wear.
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: In which season would you need a warm coat? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.4.feedback: Look outside — the trees will tell you.
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.4.narration: Which season is it where you are now? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.5.feedback: After winter, spring always comes back.
s05.science.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: Four seasons, turning round and round.
s05.science.lesson.02.title: The Four Seasons
s05.science.lesson.03.parentNote: Look at a real plant and name its parts.
s05.science.lesson.03.recap.0.prompt: Which part of a plant drinks water underground?
s05.science.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: Which of these is a part of a plant?
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: Roots drink water underground. Tap the roots.
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: Tap the stem, the leaf, and the flower.
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.2.feedback: The roots. They work underground where you cannot see.
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: Which part drinks the water? Tap it.
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.3.feedback: Carries water up, and holds the plant tall.
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.3.narration: What does the stem do? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.4.feedback: Same parts, every plant you will ever meet.
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.4.narration: Find these parts on a real plant nearby.
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.5.feedback: Each one keeps the others alive.
s05.science.lesson.03.steps.5.narration: Roots, stem, leaf, flower. Four jobs, one plant.
s05.science.lesson.03.title: Parts of a Plant
s05.science.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: A bird lives in a nest. Drag the bird to the nest.
s05.science.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: A bear lives in a den; a spider in a web.
s05.science.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: A rabbit lives in a burrow. Drag it home.
s05.science.lesson.04.steps.3.feedback: To stay safe and warm — the same reasons as you.
s05.science.lesson.04.steps.3.narration: Why do animals build homes at all? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.04.steps.4.feedback: Every animal builds what suits where it lives.
s05.science.lesson.04.steps.4.narration: Which home would you build for yourself? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.04.steps.5.feedback: None of them are wrong — just different.
s05.science.lesson.04.steps.5.narration: Nest, den, web, burrow. Four homes, four ways of living.
s05.science.lesson.04.title: Animal Homes
s05.science.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: Which one moves something away from you?
s05.science.lesson.05.steps.0.feedback: A push! It moves the door away from you.
s05.science.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: To open the door away from you, do we push or pull?
s05.science.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: To bring the wagon close, we pull.
s05.science.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: To move the box away from you — push or pull? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.05.steps.3.feedback: A hard push moves it further. Force has size!
s05.science.lesson.05.steps.3.narration: Which is stronger: a gentle push or a hard one? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.05.steps.4.narration: Push a real door, then pull it. Feel the difference.
s05.science.lesson.05.steps.5.feedback: Look for it and you will see it all day.
s05.science.lesson.05.steps.5.narration: Everything that moves was pushed or pulled.
s05.science.lesson.05.title: Push and Pull
s05.science.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: What does cold do to water?
s05.science.lesson.06.recap.1.prompt: What does warmth do to ice?
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: Cold makes water freeze into ice. Tap the freezer.
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: Warm makes ice melt back to water.
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.2.feedback: It melts faster. Heat speeds it up!
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: Leave the ice out in the sun. What happens? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.3.feedback: Yes! Back and forth, as often as you like.
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.3.narration: Can water become ice again after melting? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.4.feedback: The same water, wearing a different shape.
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.4.narration: Is melted ice a different thing, or the same water? Tap your answer.
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.5.feedback: One thing, two states. That is a big science idea.
s05.science.lesson.06.steps.5.narration: Cold makes it hard; warm makes it runny.
s05.science.lesson.06.title: Ice and Water
s05.science.quiz.01.questions.0.correctF: It floats! Cork is light for its size.
s05.science.quiz.01.questions.0.prompt: Will the cork float or sink?
s05.science.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFee: Light things often float. Try again!
s05.science.quiz.01.questions.1.correctF: It sinks. Metal is heavy and dense.
s05.science.quiz.01.questions.1.prompt: Will the metal key float or sink?
s05.science.quiz.01.questions.1.retryFee: Heavy, dense things sink. Try again!
s05.science.quiz.01.title: Sink or Float?
s05.science.quiz.02.questions.0.correctF: A plant is living. It grows.
s05.science.quiz.02.questions.0.retryFee: Living things grow and need water. Try again!
s05.science.quiz.02.title: Which Is Living?
s05.science.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFee: When is it coldest? Try again!
s05.science.quiz.03.title: Snowy Season
s05.science.quiz.04.parentNote: Ask 'does it grow?' before they answer.
s05.science.quiz.04.questions.0.retryFee: It grows, so it is living. Try again!
s05.science.quiz.04.questions.1.correctF: Non-living. It never grows or eats.
s05.science.quiz.04.questions.1.retryFee: A chair does not grow. Try again!
s05.science.quiz.04.title: Living or Not?
s05.science.story.01.pages.0.narration: A little seed sleeps in the soil. Tap to give it rain.
s05.science.story.01.pages.1.narration: With sun and water, a green sprout pokes up!
s05.science.story.01.pages.2.narration: It grows tall into a flower. Living things grow!
s05.science.story.01.title: The Little Seed
s05.science.story.02.pages.0.narration: In the morning there was a wide, shining puddle.
s05.science.story.02.pages.1.narration: By lunchtime it was only a thin, wet line.
s05.science.story.02.pages.2.narration: By evening, dry stone. The water went up into the air.
s05.science.story.02.parentNote: Watch a real puddle over one sunny day.
s05.science.story.02.title: Where the Puddle Went
s05.social.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: On a map, what does the blue part show?
s05.social.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: On a map, what does the green part show?
s05.social.lesson.01.steps.0.feedback: 'Water, like an ocean or a lake.'
s05.social.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: Tap the blue part. What is it?
s05.social.lesson.01.steps.2.narration: Tap the island — land with water all around it.
s05.social.lesson.01.steps.3.feedback: By boat or plane. The map tells you how to travel.
s05.social.lesson.01.steps.3.narration: How would you get to the island? Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.01.steps.4.feedback: More water. That is true of the real world too.
s05.social.lesson.01.steps.4.narration: Is there more land or more water on this map? Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.01.steps.5.feedback: Now you can read one anywhere.
s05.social.lesson.01.steps.5.narration: Blue is water, green is land. A map in two colours.
s05.social.lesson.01.title: Land and Water
s05.social.lesson.02.parentNote: Talk about a rule at home and why it helps.
s05.social.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: Why do we hold hands to cross the street?
s05.social.lesson.02.recap.1.prompt: Why do we take turns on the slide?
s05.social.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: We hold hands to cross the street. Tap to cross safely.
s05.social.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: We take turns on the slide. Why? To stay safe and fair.
s05.social.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: We wear a helmet on a bike. Tap the helmet.
s05.social.lesson.02.steps.3.feedback: So everyone gets a fair turn.
s05.social.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: Why do we line up instead of pushing? Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.02.steps.4.feedback: Rules are different in every home, and that is fine.
s05.social.lesson.02.steps.4.narration: What is one rule in your own home? Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: Rules are not to stop fun. They keep it going.
s05.social.lesson.02.title: Why We Have Rules
s05.social.lesson.03.recap.0.prompt: Food and water are things we…
s05.social.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: A toy is nice to have, so it is a…
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: We need food and water to live. Drag food to the 'need' box.
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.1.feedback: 'Want. Fun to have, but not a must.'
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: A toy is nice, but it's a want.
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: Water goes in the 'need' box too. Drag it over.
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.3.feedback: A need — it keeps you safe from the cold.
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.3.narration: Is a warm coat in winter a need or a want? Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.4.feedback: Wanting something is fine. Knowing the difference matters.
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.4.narration: Name one need and one want of your own. Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.5.feedback: Both are real. Only one is a must.
s05.social.lesson.03.steps.5.narration: Needs keep us alive; wants make us happy.
s05.social.lesson.03.title: Needs and Wants
s05.social.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: A farmer grows our food. Tap the farmer.
s05.social.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: Tap the nurse and the bus driver.
s05.social.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: Tap the teacher and the builder.
s05.social.lesson.04.steps.3.feedback: The bus driver. Jobs connect to each other.
s05.social.lesson.04.steps.3.narration: Whose job helps you get to school? Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.04.steps.4.feedback: You can change your mind as many times as you like.
s05.social.lesson.04.steps.4.narration: What job would you like to try one day? Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.04.steps.5.feedback: That is what a town really is.
s05.social.lesson.04.steps.5.narration: Every job here holds up somebody else's day.
s05.social.lesson.04.title: Jobs People Do
s05.social.lesson.05.parentNote: Show your child your country's flag and its colors.
s05.social.lesson.05.recap.1.prompt: What do flags have on them?
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: Every country has a flag. Tap to wave one.
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: Flags have colors and shapes. What's on yours?
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.2.feedback: Stars, stripes, circles — flags use shapes.
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: Tap the flag with a star on it.
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.3.feedback: So people can recognise it and feel it is theirs.
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.3.narration: Why does a country have a flag at all? Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.4.feedback: Your colours, your shapes, your choice.
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.4.narration: Make a flag for your own family on paper.
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.5.feedback: Every country has one, and now so do you.
s05.social.lesson.05.steps.5.narration: A flag is a picture that says 'this is us'.
s05.social.lesson.05.title: My Flag
s05.social.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: Long ago, what did people ride?
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: Long ago, people rode horses. Tap the horse.
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: Today, we ride in cars. Tap the car.
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.2.feedback: Days of walking for one message!
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: Long ago, letters went by hand. Tap the messenger.
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.3.feedback: A second. That is a very big change.
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.3.narration: How long does a message take today? Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.4.feedback: They lived through the change themselves!
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.4.narration: Ask a grown-up what was different when they were small. Tap your answer.
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.5.feedback: The world keeps changing, and you are in it.
s05.social.lesson.06.steps.5.narration: Things that seem normal now were once brand new.
s05.social.lesson.06.title: Long Ago and Today
s05.social.quiz.01.questions.0.correctFe: A stop sign means stop and look.
s05.social.quiz.01.questions.0.prompt: What does the red stop sign mean?
s05.social.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFeed: Red usually means stop. Try again!
s05.social.quiz.01.title: Safety Signs
s05.social.quiz.02.questions.0.correctFe: Water is a need. We must have it.
s05.social.quiz.02.questions.0.prompt: Is water a need or a want?
s05.social.quiz.02.questions.0.retryFeed: Could you live without it? Try again!
s05.social.quiz.02.title: Need or Want?
s05.social.quiz.03.questions.0.correctFe: Stop and look. That's what red means.
s05.social.quiz.03.questions.0.prompt: What does a red stop sign mean?
s05.social.quiz.03.title: Stop Sign
s05.social.quiz.04.parentNote: Ask 'could we live without it?' each time.
s05.social.quiz.04.questions.0.correctFe: A need. Nobody lives without it.
s05.social.quiz.04.questions.0.prompt: Is water a need or a want?
s05.social.quiz.04.questions.0.retryFeed: We cannot live without water. Try again!
s05.social.quiz.04.questions.1.correctFe: A want. Lovely to have, not a must.
s05.social.quiz.04.questions.1.retryFeed: We can live without toys. Try again!
s05.social.quiz.04.title: Need or Want?
s05.social.story.01.pages.0.narration: Mr. Ade's groceries spilled on the path.
s05.social.story.01.pages.1.narration: Nia and Sam stop to help pick them up.
s05.social.story.01.pages.2.narration: 'Thank you!' he smiles. Helping makes a happy street.
s05.social.story.01.parentNote: Talk about a time your family helped a neighbor.
s05.social.story.01.title: Helping My Neighbor
s05.social.story.02.pages.0.narration: Everyone wanted the swing at once. Nobody got a turn.
s05.social.story.02.pages.1.narration: So we sat down and made a rule: count to twenty, then swap.
s05.social.story.02.pages.2.narration: After that, everybody got a turn. The rule was ours.
s05.social.story.02.parentNote: Agree one small house rule together this week.
s05.social.story.02.title: The Rule We Made Together
s06.math.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: 2 ten-rods and 3 ones make which number?
s06.math.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: 1 ten and 4 ones make which number?
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: Make the number 23. Drag 2 ten-rods and 3 ones.
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.2.narration: Now make 31. Drag 3 ten-rods and 1 one.
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.3.feedback: Where a digit sits tells you its job.
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.3.narration: Watch: in 45, the 4 counts tens and the 5 counts ones.
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.4.narration: Make 50. How many ten-rods, and how many ones?
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.5.feedback: A pile of ten is one ten. 2 tens is 20!
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.5.narration: These 20 coins sit in 2 piles of ten. Tap one pile of ten.
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.6.feedback: 6! The last digit counts the ones.
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.7.feedback: Place value. You read it like a mathematician.
s06.math.lesson.01.steps.7.narration: Every number you write is tens and ones.
s06.math.lesson.01.title: Tens and Ones
s06.math.lesson.02.recap.1.prompt: Counting on from 6 by three gets you to…
s06.math.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: 6 and 3 more. Tap to count on.
s06.math.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: Now count on: 5 and 4 more. Tap each one as you count.
s06.math.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: Watch the quick way: start at the bigger number and count on.
s06.math.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: 3 red apples and 4 green apples in the basket. Tap the basket to add them.
s06.math.lesson.02.steps.6.feedback: 8! You added without counting every one.
s06.math.lesson.02.steps.7.feedback: Adding is just counting on. Well done.
s06.math.lesson.02.steps.7.narration: You can add any two numbers up to ten.
s06.math.lesson.02.title: Add to 10
s06.math.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: If 4 of 10 birds fly away, how many are left?
s06.math.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: 10 birds. 4 fly away. Tap to take them away.
s06.math.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: 8 apples. Take away 3. Tap the ones that go.
s06.math.lesson.03.steps.3.feedback: Count back, not up. That is the difference.
s06.math.lesson.03.steps.3.narration: Watch: to subtract, count back from the big number.
s06.math.lesson.03.steps.5.narration: 7 coins in your hand. You spend 2. Tap the 2 coins that go.
s06.math.lesson.03.steps.7.feedback: You subtract like a mathematician now.
s06.math.lesson.03.steps.7.narration: Take away means fewer than you started with.
s06.math.lesson.03.title: Subtract from 10
s06.math.lesson.04.steps.3.feedback: That is why they all start with a 1.
s06.math.lesson.04.steps.3.narration: Every teen number is one ten, plus some ones.
s06.math.lesson.04.steps.4.narration: One ten and 5 ones. What number is that?
s06.math.lesson.04.steps.5.narration: Drag 1 ten-rod and 7 cubes to build a teen number.
s06.math.lesson.04.steps.6.feedback: 9! Nineteen is one ten and nine ones.
s06.math.lesson.04.steps.7.narration: Teen numbers stop hiding once you see the ten.
s06.math.lesson.04.title: Teen Numbers
s06.math.lesson.05.parentNote: Count groups of ten with small objects at home.
s06.math.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: Break 14 into tens and ones. How many ones?
s06.math.lesson.05.recap.1.prompt: 1 ten and 2 ones make which number?
s06.math.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: 14 is 1 ten and 4 ones. Drag a ten-stick and 4 cubes.
s06.math.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: Now make 26. Drag 2 ten-sticks and 6 cubes.
s06.math.lesson.05.steps.3.feedback: Ten ones make one ten. Always.
s06.math.lesson.05.steps.3.narration: Watch: swap ten loose cubes for one ten-stick. Same amount.
s06.math.lesson.05.steps.5.feedback: 3 tens is 30. Counting in tens is faster!
s06.math.lesson.05.steps.5.narration: A box holds 10 blocks. Tap 3 boxes to show 30 blocks.
s06.math.lesson.05.steps.7.feedback: You can build any number now.
s06.math.lesson.05.steps.7.narration: Big numbers are just tens and ones in a row.
s06.math.lesson.05.title: Tens and Ones
s06.math.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: A circle is which kind of shape?
s06.math.lesson.06.recap.1.prompt: A cube is which kind of shape?
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: A circle is flat (2D). A ball is solid (3D). Tap the flat circle.
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: A square is flat. A box is solid. Tap the flat square.
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.3.narration: Watch: flat shapes you draw. Solid shapes you can hold.
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.4.feedback: The ball! You can hold a solid.
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.4.narration: Tap the shape you could pick up: a triangle drawn on paper, or a ball.
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.5.feedback: A cup, a box, a ball. Solids are everywhere!
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.5.narration: A cup on the shelf is a solid shape too. Tap the cup.
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.6.narration: Is a circle drawn on paper flat or solid? Tap flat.
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.7.feedback: You can sort every shape you meet.
s06.math.lesson.06.steps.7.narration: A drawn circle is 2D. A ball is 3D.
s06.math.lesson.06.title: 2D and 3D Shapes
s06.math.quiz.01.parentNote: A ten-frame shows a number as 'ten and some more'. Ask how many empty squares are left — that is the same question as what makes ten.
s06.math.quiz.01.questions.0.correctFeed: You read the ten-frame. That is 7.
s06.math.quiz.01.questions.0.prompt: How many counters are on the ten-frame?
s06.math.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFeedba: Count the filled squares. Try again!
s06.math.quiz.01.questions.2.prompt: The frame holds 7. How many empty squares are left?
s06.math.quiz.01.questions.2.retryFeedba: A full frame is ten. Count the gaps!
s06.math.quiz.01.questions.3.correctFeed: 9 is more. It fills more of the frame.
s06.math.quiz.01.questions.3.retryFeedba: Which one fills more squares? Try again!
s06.math.quiz.01.title: Ten-Frame Match
s06.math.quiz.02.parentNote: If they count from one every time, show them counting on from the bigger number. It is the single biggest speed-up at this age.
s06.math.quiz.02.questions.1.retryFeedba: Start at 5 and count on four. Try again!
s06.math.quiz.02.questions.2.correctFeed: 7 and 3 make ten. A number bond!
s06.math.quiz.02.questions.2.retryFeedba: How many more does 7 need to reach 10? Try again!
s06.math.quiz.02.questions.3.correctFeed: 8. Doubles are worth learning by heart.
s06.math.quiz.02.questions.3.prompt: 4 + 4 is a double. What is it?
s06.math.quiz.02.questions.3.retryFeedba: Two fours. Count them all. Try again!
s06.math.quiz.02.title: Add It
s06.math.quiz.03.parentNote: Counting back is harder than counting on. Let them use fingers for as long as they need — speed comes later.
s06.math.quiz.03.questions.2.correctFeed: Zero. Take away all of them and none are left.
s06.math.quiz.03.questions.2.prompt: 7 birds sit on a branch. 7 fly away. How many are left?
s06.math.quiz.03.questions.2.retryFeedba: All of them flew. How many stayed? Try again!
s06.math.quiz.03.questions.3.correctFeed: 9 - 6 takes away six, and leaves the least.
s06.math.quiz.03.questions.3.prompt: Which one takes away the most?
s06.math.quiz.03.questions.3.retryFeedba: Which number is being taken away? Try again!
s06.math.quiz.03.title: Take Away
s06.math.quiz.04.parentNote: Place value is the idea that a digit's position changes its worth. Point at house numbers and ask which digit is the tens.
s06.math.quiz.04.questions.0.correctFeed: 3 tens and 4 ones. The first digit counts tens.
s06.math.quiz.04.questions.0.retryFeedba: Look at the first digit. Try again!
s06.math.quiz.04.questions.1.prompt: 2 tens and 7 ones make which number?
s06.math.quiz.04.questions.1.retryFeedba: Tens go first when we write it. Try again!
s06.math.quiz.04.questions.2.correctFeed: 41. Same digits, but 4 tens beats 1 ten.
s06.math.quiz.04.questions.2.retryFeedba: Compare the tens first. Try again!
s06.math.quiz.04.questions.3.correctFeed: Zero ones. Fifty is 5 tens exactly.
s06.math.quiz.04.questions.3.retryFeedba: What does the last digit say? Try again!
s06.math.quiz.04.title: Tens and Ones
s06.math.story.01.pages.0.narration: A bear balances 3 apples on top of his head.
s06.math.story.01.pages.1.narration: 'I can carry more,' says the bear. Tap to add 2 more.
s06.math.story.01.pages.3.narration: A bird lands on the very top apple. The tower leans.
s06.math.story.01.pages.4.narration: The bear stands very still. Slowly, the tower straightens.
s06.math.story.01.pages.5.narration: They all stay up. Hooray for 5 apples and one brave bird!
s06.math.story.01.parentNote: Pause on each page and let them count before the narrator does. The wobble is the fun part.
s06.math.story.01.title: Ten Apples on Top
s06.math.story.02.pages.0.narration: Amina has 24 beans to sell at the market.
s06.math.story.02.pages.1.narration: She puts ten in one cup, ten in another. Two cups of ten.
s06.math.story.02.pages.2.narration: Four beans are left over. 2 tens and 4 ones is 24.
s06.math.story.02.pages.3.narration: A customer buys one whole cup. How many beans is that?
s06.math.story.02.pages.4.narration: Ten! Now Amina has 1 ten and 4 ones. Fourteen beans.
s06.math.story.02.pages.5.narration: Counting in tens is faster than counting one by one. Amina knew that all along.
s06.math.story.02.parentNote: Real coins on the table turn this from a story into a lesson. Ten singles for one ten is the whole idea.
s06.math.story.02.title: The Market Stall
s06.reading.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: How many sounds do the letters s and h make together?
s06.reading.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: Which word ends with that shhh sound?
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.2.narration: Tap 'shop'. Listen for shhh at the start.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.3.feedback: Two letters, one sound. That is a digraph.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.3.narration: Watch: s and h stand together and make one new sound.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.4.feedback: Sock! It starts with s on its own.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.4.narration: One of these has no 'sh': shell, shoe, sock. Tap the odd one.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.5.feedback: wa-sh. Wash! Same sound, other end.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.5.narration: 'sh' can end a word too. Tap 'wash'.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.6.feedback: The start. You heard it first.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.6.narration: Where is the 'sh' in 'shell' — start or end? Tap the start.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.7.feedback: Shhh. That is a reader's ear.
s06.reading.lesson.01.steps.7.narration: You can hear 'sh' anywhere in a word now.
s06.reading.lesson.01.title: Digraph: sh
s06.reading.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: Which word starts with the ch sound?
s06.reading.lesson.02.recap.1.prompt: Which word ends with the ch sound?
s06.reading.lesson.02.steps.3.feedback: Another digraph. Two letters, one sound.
s06.reading.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: Watch: the letters c and h together say ch, not c then h.
s06.reading.lesson.02.steps.4.narration: Tap the word that starts with ch: cat, chair, cup.
s06.reading.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: 'ch' comes at the end too. Tap 'much'.
s06.reading.lesson.02.steps.6.feedback: Chip. ch and sh are different sounds!
s06.reading.lesson.02.steps.6.narration: Which starts with ch, 'chip' or 'ship'? Tap 'chip'.
s06.reading.lesson.02.steps.7.narration: sh and ch are two sounds you own now.
s06.reading.lesson.02.title: Digraph: ch
s06.reading.lesson.03.recap.0.prompt: Which of these is a sight word from this lesson?
s06.reading.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: Sight words are ones we should read…
s06.reading.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: Tap 'you' again, fast. No sounding out.
s06.reading.lesson.03.steps.3.feedback: Sight words. Know them by their shape.
s06.reading.lesson.03.steps.3.narration: Some words we read whole, because their letters play tricks.
s06.reading.lesson.03.steps.4.feedback: 'I see you!' Three sight words in a row.
s06.reading.lesson.03.steps.4.narration: Read: 'I see you.' Tap each word.
s06.reading.lesson.03.steps.5.feedback: 'go'. You spotted it in a sentence!
s06.reading.lesson.03.steps.5.narration: Find 'go' in this line: 'We go home.' Tap it.
s06.reading.lesson.03.steps.7.narration: You, see, go — read without stopping.
s06.reading.lesson.03.title: Sight Words: you, see, go
s06.reading.lesson.04.recap.0.prompt: Which word tells you the size of the fish?
s06.reading.lesson.04.recap.1.prompt: In the sentence about the dog, what could it do?
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.0.feedback: 'The dog can run!' You read it!
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: Read: 'The dog can run.' Tap each word.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.1.feedback: 'I see a big fish!' Great reading.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: Read: 'The cat is on the mat.' Tap each word.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.3.feedback: That is how a sentence works.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.3.narration: Watch: read left to right, one word at a time, then stop at the dot.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.4.feedback: You used a sight word and a digraph in one line!
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.4.narration: Read: 'We go to the shop.' Tap each word.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.5.feedback: Right — it does not tell us anything yet.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.5.narration: One of these is not a sentence. Tap 'the big red'.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.6.feedback: 'hot'. You read for meaning, not just sound.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.6.narration: In 'The sun is hot.', tap the word that tells us about the sun.
s06.reading.lesson.04.steps.7.narration: You read whole sentences on your own.
s06.reading.lesson.04.title: Read a Sentence
s06.reading.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: Which letters spell cat, in order?
s06.reading.lesson.05.recap.1.prompt: Which letters spell sun, in order?
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: Spell 'cat'. Drag c, a, t in order.
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.2.feedback: sh-i-p. Ship! The sh goes together.
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: Spell 'ship'. Drag s, h, i, p in order.
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.3.feedback: Slow speech shows you the letters.
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.3.narration: Watch: say the word slowly, and write the sound you hear first.
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.4.feedback: One letter changed the whole word!
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.4.narration: Spell 'hat'. Then change one letter to make 'mat'.
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.5.feedback: ch-i-p. Chip! You used a digraph.
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.6.narration: Which letter is missing: c _ t, for a cat? Tap 'a'.
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.7.feedback: Writers hear sounds and choose letters.
s06.reading.lesson.05.steps.7.narration: You can build words, not just read them.
s06.reading.lesson.05.title: Build a Word
s06.reading.lesson.06.recap.1.prompt: What does a period tell the reader to do?
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: A sentence starts with a big letter. Tap the capital T.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: It ends with a period. Tap the dot.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: Find the capital letter in 'My dog naps.' Tap it.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.3.feedback: Two little signs that hold a sentence together.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.3.narration: Watch: a capital says start here, a period says stop.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.4.feedback: At the very end. Now it stops properly.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.4.narration: This sentence is missing its period. Tap where it should go.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.5.feedback: The second one. Big letter, then a dot.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.5.narration: Tap the sentence written correctly: 'the sun is hot.' or 'The sun is hot.'
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.6.feedback: 'S' for Sam. Names always start big.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.6.narration: Names get capitals too. Tap the capital in 'Sam has a hat.'
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.7.feedback: You write like a writer now.
s06.reading.lesson.06.steps.7.narration: Capital at the start, period at the end.
s06.reading.lesson.06.title: Capitals and Periods
s06.reading.quiz.01.parentNote: Two rules carry most early writing: start big, end with a mark. Point them out on cereal boxes and signs.
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.0.correctF: You checked both ends. Capital letter and a period.
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFee: A sentence starts big and ends with a dot. Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.1.correctF: A period. It tells the reader to stop.
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.1.prompt: What goes at the end of a telling sentence?
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.1.retryFee: Which one means stop? Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.2.correctF: Sam is a name, and names always start big.
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.2.prompt: Which word needs a capital letter?
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.2.retryFee: Which one is somebody's name? Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.3.correctF: Both ends. Big letter at the start, mark at the end.
A capital and an end mark
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.3.prompt: 'is the sun hot' — what is missing?
s06.reading.quiz.01.questions.3.retryFee: Look at the very start and the very end. Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.01.title: Capitals and End Marks
s06.reading.quiz.02.parentNote: A digraph is two letters making one sound. Say the word slowly and let them listen rather than look.
s06.reading.quiz.02.questions.1.correctF: Chair. The c and h say ch together.
s06.reading.quiz.02.questions.1.retryFee: Say each one aloud. Which begins ch? Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.02.questions.2.correctF: One. Two letters, one sound. That is a digraph.
s06.reading.quiz.02.questions.2.retryFee: Say shhh. Is that one sound or two? Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.02.questions.3.correctF: Lunch. A digraph can end a word too.
s06.reading.quiz.02.questions.3.retryFee: Listen to the last sound. Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.02.title: Find the Digraph
s06.reading.quiz.03.parentNote: This is comprehension, not decoding: the wrong answers are readable too. Ask 'does that make sense?' rather than 'is that right?'.
s06.reading.quiz.03.questions.0.correctF: 'The sun is hot.' That one fits.
s06.reading.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFee: Which word makes sense? Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.03.questions.1.correctF: 'I can read the book.' A doing word fits there.
s06.reading.quiz.03.questions.1.prompt: 'I can ___ the book.' Which word fits?
s06.reading.quiz.03.questions.1.retryFee: What can you do to a book? Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.03.questions.2.correctF: 'The fish can swim.' That is what fish do.
s06.reading.quiz.03.questions.2.retryFee: What does a fish do in water? Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.03.questions.3.correctF: The first one tells us something whole.
s06.reading.quiz.03.questions.3.retryFee: Which one finishes its idea? Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.03.title: Finish the Sentence
s06.reading.quiz.04.parentNote: Sight words break the usual sounding-out rules, so they are learned by shape. Five seconds a day beats a long session once a week.
s06.reading.quiz.04.questions.0.retryFee: Look at the whole shape of the word. Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.04.questions.1.retryFee: Which one has a double e? Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.04.questions.2.correctF: Four. Spaces show where each word ends.
s06.reading.quiz.04.questions.2.prompt: Read this line: 'We go to school.' How many words?
s06.reading.quiz.04.questions.2.retryFee: Count the spaces between them. Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.04.questions.3.correctF: Right. Sounding out 'you' does not work.
Their letters do not sound out normally
s06.reading.quiz.04.questions.3.prompt: Why do we learn sight words by shape?
s06.reading.quiz.04.questions.3.retryFee: Try sounding out 'you' letter by letter. Try again!
s06.reading.quiz.04.title: Sight Words
s06.reading.story.01.pages.0.narration: Sam has a red hat. (Tap any word to hear it.)
s06.reading.story.01.pages.1.narration: The hat is on the mat.
s06.reading.story.01.pages.2.narration: A cat sits on the hat!
s06.reading.story.01.pages.3.narration: 'Get off, cat,' says Sam. The cat does not get off.
s06.reading.story.01.pages.4.narration: Sam sits down on the mat and waits.
s06.reading.story.01.pages.5.narration: Sam and the cat sit on the mat. The end!
s06.reading.story.01.parentNote: Every word here can be sounded out except 'the'. Let them do the work and only step in on that one.
s06.reading.story.01.title: Sam and the Red Hat
s06.reading.story.02.pages.0.narration: In the shed there is a ship. It is small and it is red.
s06.reading.story.02.pages.1.narration: Chad finds the ship. 'Can it go on the water?' he asks.
s06.reading.story.02.pages.2.narration: There is a chip in the ship. Water gets in.
s06.reading.story.02.pages.3.narration: Chad gets a patch. He fits it on the chip.
s06.reading.story.02.pages.4.narration: The ship sits on the water. It does not sink!
s06.reading.story.02.pages.5.narration: Chad and the ship go up the river. Shhh — off they go.
s06.reading.story.02.parentNote: Count the 'sh' and 'ch' words together on a second read. Hunting for a sound fixes it faster than drilling it.
s06.reading.story.02.title: The Ship in the Shed
s06.science.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: Ice is hard and keeps its shape. Which state is it?
s06.science.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: Steam floats away into the air. Which state is it?
s06.science.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: Ice is hard. What state is it?
s06.science.lesson.01.steps.3.narration: Watch: solids hold their shape, liquids pour, gases float away.
s06.science.lesson.01.steps.4.narration: A rock sits in your hand and keeps its shape. Tap solid.
s06.science.lesson.01.steps.5.narration: Milk in a cup takes the shape of the cup. Tap liquid.
s06.science.lesson.01.steps.6.narration: Ice on a warm day turns to water. Tap what it became.
s06.science.lesson.01.steps.7.narration: Solid, liquid, gas — the same water can be all three.
s06.science.lesson.01.title: Solid, Liquid, Gas
s06.science.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: Which two things do animals need to live?
s06.science.lesson.02.recap.1.prompt: A den or a nest gives an animal…
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: Animals need food and water. Tap the food and water.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: They need shelter, too. Tap the den.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.2.feedback: Air to breathe. Every animal needs it!
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: Animals need air too. Tap the breeze.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.3.feedback: Needs, not wants. A toy is not a need.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: Watch: food, water, air, shelter. Four needs, every animal.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.4.feedback: Shelter! A nest keeps the eggs safe.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.4.narration: A bird builds a nest. Tap the need that fills.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.5.feedback: Water! The river is its home and its drink.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: A fish lives in the river. Tap what it takes from there.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.6.feedback: A ball is fun, but nothing lives on it.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.6.narration: Which is not a need: water, food, or a ball? Tap the ball.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.7.feedback: Now you know what keeps a creature alive.
s06.science.lesson.02.steps.7.narration: Every animal needs the same four things.
s06.science.lesson.02.title: What Animals Need
s06.science.lesson.03.recap.0.prompt: What gives us daytime and warmth?
s06.science.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: What do we see shining at night?
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: The sun gives us day and warmth. Tap the sun.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: The moon and stars shine at night. Tap them.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.2.feedback: Our own star. That is why it looks so big!
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: The sun is a star, very close to us. Tap the sun.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.3.feedback: The earth turns, so day follows night.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.3.narration: Watch: the sun lights the day, the moon shines at night.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.4.narration: Stars are up there in the day too, hidden by sunlight. Tap the sky.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.5.feedback: The same moon, lit from a new angle.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.5.narration: The moon changes shape through the month. Tap tonight's moon.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.6.feedback: The sun. The moon has no heat of its own.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.6.narration: Which gives us warmth: the sun or the moon? Tap the sun.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.7.feedback: Look up tonight and find one.
s06.science.lesson.03.steps.7.narration: Sun, moon and stars — you can name the sky.
s06.science.lesson.03.title: Sun, Moon, Stars
s06.science.lesson.04.parentNote: Pick clothes together based on today's weather.
s06.science.lesson.04.recap.0.prompt: What do you wear on a cold, snowy day?
s06.science.lesson.04.recap.1.prompt: What do you wear on a hot, sunny day?
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: It's cold and snowy. Drag the warm coat.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: It's hot and sunny. Drag the sun hat.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: It is raining. Drag the umbrella.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.3.feedback: Clothes are how people handle the sky.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.3.narration: Watch: we dress for the weather so our body stays comfortable.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.4.narration: Windy and cool today. Drag the scarf.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.5.feedback: You read today's weather and chose. That is science!
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.5.narration: Look outside now. Tap the coat or the hat for today.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.6.feedback: No — you would be far too hot.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.6.narration: Would you wear a warm coat on a hot sunny day? Tap no.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.7.feedback: You can dress yourself for any sky.
s06.science.lesson.04.steps.7.narration: Weather changes, and so do we.
s06.science.lesson.04.title: Weather and Clothes
s06.science.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: A chair can be made of which material?
s06.science.lesson.05.recap.1.prompt: Which material is a spoon often made of?
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: A chair can be wood. Tap the wood.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: A spoon can be metal; a cup plastic. Tap them.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.2.feedback: Glass! We can see straight through it.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: Glass is clear and hard. Tap the glass window.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.3.feedback: A chair might be wood, metal and cloth together.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.3.narration: Watch: one chair can be made of wood, metal and cloth at once.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.4.narration: Paper comes from trees, like wood. Tap the paper.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.5.feedback: Cloth! Soft, and it soaks up water.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.5.narration: Cloth is soft and bends. Tap the cloth towel.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.6.feedback: Glass. Materials are chosen for the job.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.6.narration: Which would you use for a window: wood or glass? Tap glass.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.7.feedback: You can name what things are made of now.
s06.science.lesson.05.steps.7.narration: Every cup, chair and book is made of something.
s06.science.lesson.05.title: What's It Made Of?
s06.science.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: How does a race car move?
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: A race car moves fast. Tap it.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: A snail moves slow. Tap it.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: A cheetah runs fast. A turtle walks slow. Tap the fast one.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.3.feedback: Speed is distance and time together.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.3.narration: Watch: fast means more distance in the same time.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.4.narration: You walk, then you run. Tap the faster one.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.5.narration: A river runs fast after rain and slow in dry weather. Tap the fast river.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.6.feedback: The snail. A bike wins every time.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.6.narration: Which is slower: a snail or a bike? Tap the snail.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.7.feedback: That is measuring, without a ruler.
s06.science.lesson.06.steps.7.narration: Fast and slow — you can compare any two things.
s06.science.lesson.06.title: Fast and Slow
s06.science.quiz.01.parentNote: Groups are defined by body features, not by where the animal lives. A whale swims but is still a mammal.
s06.science.quiz.01.questions.0.correctF: A dog is a mammal. Mammals have fur and feed milk.
s06.science.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFee: Does a dog have fur? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.01.questions.1.retryFee: Feathers and wings mean... try again!
s06.science.quiz.01.questions.2.correctF: Reptiles. A snake and a lizard both belong there.
s06.science.quiz.01.questions.2.prompt: Which animal group has scales and lays eggs on land?
s06.science.quiz.01.questions.2.retryFee: Think of a snake. What is its skin like? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.01.questions.3.correctF: A mammal. It breathes air and feeds its young milk.
s06.science.quiz.01.questions.3.prompt: A whale lives in the sea. Is it a fish?
s06.science.quiz.01.questions.3.retryFee: Where an animal lives is not its group. Try again!
s06.science.quiz.01.title: Mammal, Bird, Reptile, or Fish?
s06.science.quiz.02.parentNote: The needs/wants split is the whole lesson. A pet is a good place to make it concrete.
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.0.prompt: Which does an animal need to live?
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.0.retryFee: What can't they live without? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.1.correctF: Shelter. A safe place for eggs and chicks.
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.1.prompt: What does a nest give a bird?
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.1.retryFee: Is a nest something to eat? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.2.correctF: A toy is nice, but nothing lives on it.
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.2.prompt: Which is a want, not a need?
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.2.retryFee: Which one could you live without? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.3.correctF: Four: food, water, air and shelter.
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.3.prompt: How many needs does every animal share?
s06.science.quiz.02.questions.3.retryFee: Food, water, air and one more. Try again!
s06.science.quiz.02.title: Animal Needs
s06.science.quiz.03.parentNote: Materials are chosen for a job — glass to see through, cloth to be soft. Ask why, not just what.
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.0.correctF: The log is made of wood.
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.0.prompt: Which one is made of wood?
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFee: Which comes from a tree? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.1.correctF: Right. The material is chosen for the job.
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.1.prompt: Why do we make windows from glass?
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.1.retryFee: What can you do through a window? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.2.correctF: Trees. Paper is wood, squashed and dried.
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.2.retryFee: Wood and paper come from the same place. Try again!
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.3.correctF: Cloth. Soft, warm, and it bends with you.
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.3.prompt: Which material would you choose for a warm coat?
s06.science.quiz.03.questions.3.retryFee: Which one would you want against your skin? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.03.title: What Is It Made Of?
s06.science.quiz.04.parentNote: Water is the best example because a child can watch it be all three. Ice in a warm glass does the whole lesson.
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.0.correctF: Solid. It holds its own shape.
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.0.prompt: Ice is hard and keeps its shape. What state is it?
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.0.retryFee: Can you hold it without a cup? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.1.correctF: Liquid. It pours and fills whatever holds it.
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.1.prompt: Milk takes the shape of its cup. What state is it?
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.1.retryFee: Does it keep its own shape? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.2.correctF: Gas. It spreads out and floats away.
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.2.prompt: Steam rises off a hot pot. What state is it?
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.2.retryFee: Can you catch it in your hand? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.3.correctF: Still water. Heat changed its state, not its stuff.
Its state, not what it is
s06.science.quiz.04.questions.3.retryFee: Freeze it again — what do you get? Try again!
s06.science.quiz.04.title: Solid, Liquid, Gas
s06.science.story.01.pages.0.narration: The sun warms the lake. Water rises up as invisible mist.
s06.science.story.01.pages.1.narration: Up high the air is cold. The mist turns back into tiny drops.
s06.science.story.01.pages.2.narration: Millions of drops together make a cloud. The cloud grows heavy.
s06.science.story.01.pages.3.narration: Too heavy to float. Drip-drop — it rains back down!
s06.science.story.01.pages.4.narration: The rain runs into the river, and the river runs to the lake.
s06.science.story.01.pages.5.narration: Then the sun warms the lake again. Water goes round and round.
s06.science.story.01.parentNote: Watch for clouds and rain together and talk about the cycle. A steamy kettle or a cold window shows the same thing indoors.
s06.science.story.01.title: Where Does Rain Come From?
s06.science.story.02.pages.0.narration: A cheetah can run faster than any animal on land.
s06.science.story.02.pages.1.narration: A snail moves so slowly you can barely see it move at all.
s06.science.story.02.pages.2.narration: 'Race me,' says the cheetah, and off he goes in a blur.
s06.science.story.02.pages.3.narration: But a cheetah can only run fast for a very short time.
s06.science.story.02.pages.4.narration: He stops to rest under a tree. The snail keeps going.
s06.science.story.02.pages.5.narration: Fast is not always first. Slow and steady arrives too.
s06.science.story.02.parentNote: Slow is not the same as bad at something. That is the point of the ending — worth saying out loud.
s06.science.story.02.title: The Snail and the Cheetah
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.0.feedback: 'A flag is a symbol of a country.'
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: Tap the flag to see it wave.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.1.feedback: 'An anthem is a country's special song.'
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.1.narration: Tap the music note to hear an anthem.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.2.feedback: Flags use colour and shape to mean a place.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.2.narration: Every country has its own flag. Tap a flag you know.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.3.feedback: Symbols. They stand for something bigger.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.3.narration: Watch: a flag is a picture of a country, and an anthem is its song.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.4.narration: People stand still when the anthem plays. Tap to stand.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.5.feedback: Those colours mean something to everyone who lives there.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.5.narration: Tap the colours on your country's flag.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.6.feedback: A song. The flag is the picture.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.6.narration: Is an anthem a song or a picture? Tap song.
s06.social.lesson.01.steps.7.narration: A flag and an anthem belong to everyone in a country.
s06.social.lesson.01.title: Our Flag and Anthem
s06.social.lesson.02.parentNote: Notice and name good citizenship in daily life.
s06.social.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: What does a good citizen do for others?
s06.social.lesson.02.recap.1.prompt: Taking turns and giving some to a friend is called…
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: Good citizens help others. Tap to help carry books.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: They share and follow rules. Tap to share.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.2.feedback: In the bin. The street is better for everyone!
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: Good citizens keep places clean. Tap the litter to bin it.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.3.feedback: Small acts, done by many, change a whole community.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: Watch: a citizen is someone who belongs to a place and helps it.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.4.feedback: You helped without being asked. That counts most.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.4.narration: Someone drops their books. Tap to help.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.5.feedback: Waiting is fair. Fair is what rules are for.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: Rules keep everybody safe. Tap to wait your turn.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.6.feedback: No — it leaves work for someone else.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.6.narration: Is littering good citizenship? Tap no.
s06.social.lesson.02.steps.7.feedback: That is what a good citizen does.
s06.social.lesson.02.title: Being a Good Citizen
s06.social.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: What do maps help us do?
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: A map shows things from above, looking down. Tap the bed on the room map.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: Tap the door on the map.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.2.feedback: There it is, seen from above!
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: Tap the window on the room map.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.3.feedback: A map is the world from above, made small.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.3.narration: Watch: stand on a chair and look down. That view is a map.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.4.feedback: Maps use small pictures for real places.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.4.narration: This map shows a school and a street. Tap the school.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.5.feedback: You just made a route. That is what maps are for!
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.5.narration: Trace a route from the door to the bed. Tap the path.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.6.narration: Does a map show things from the side or from above? Tap above.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.7.feedback: You can find your way now.
s06.social.lesson.03.steps.7.narration: Maps turn a place into a picture you can read.
s06.social.lesson.03.title: A Map from Above
s06.social.lesson.04.recap.0.prompt: Bread is something you can hold, so it is a…
s06.social.lesson.04.recap.1.prompt: A haircut is work done for you, so it is a…
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: Bread is a good. Something we can hold. Drag it to 'goods'.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: A haircut is a service. Something done for us. Drag it to 'services'.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.2.feedback: A good! You can hold a shoe.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: A shoe is a good. Drag it to 'goods'.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.3.feedback: Can you hold it, or is it done for you? That is the test.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.3.narration: Watch: goods are things, services are jobs done for you.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.4.feedback: A service! Teaching is work, not a thing.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.4.narration: A teacher teaching is a service. Drag it to 'services'.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.5.feedback: Coins buy goods and services alike.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.5.narration: Money buys both. Tap the coins.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.6.feedback: A service. Nothing to carry home.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.6.narration: Is a doctor's visit a good or a service? Tap service.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.7.feedback: Now you can sort any job or thing.
s06.social.lesson.04.steps.7.narration: Bread is a good you hold. A haircut is a service done for you.
s06.social.lesson.04.title: Goods and Services
s06.social.lesson.05.parentNote: Share a food, song, or word from your family's culture.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: Children around the world eat different foods. Tap to explore.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.1.feedback: Our world is full of cultures!
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: We wear different clothes and speak different languages. All special.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: Children everywhere play. Tap the ball game you know.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.3.feedback: Everyone needs food, shelter and family.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.3.narration: Watch: homes, food and clothes differ, but needs are the same.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.4.narration: Some homes are tall, some are round. Tap a house unlike yours.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.5.feedback: Hello sounds different everywhere, and means the same!
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.5.narration: Say hello in a new language. Tap to hear one.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.6.feedback: Yes. Needs are the same everywhere.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.6.narration: Do children in other countries need food too? Tap yes.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.7.feedback: That is a big idea, and you have it.
s06.social.lesson.05.steps.7.narration: Many ways to live. One world.
s06.social.lesson.05.title: People Around the World
s06.social.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: Long ago, people wrote letters with a…
s06.social.lesson.06.recap.1.prompt: What happens to tools over time?
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: Long ago, people wrote letters by hand. Tap the quill pen.
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: Now we can send a message on a phone. Tap the phone.
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: Long ago, people washed clothes by hand. Tap the old way.
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.3.feedback: People still write and wash. Only the how changed.
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.3.narration: Watch: tools change, but the job stays the same.
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.4.narration: Long ago a horse pulled a cart. Now a car drives. Tap the car.
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.5.feedback: History is in your own family!
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.5.narration: Ask a grown-up what they used before a phone. Tap the phone.
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.6.feedback: The quill. Ink and a feather!
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.6.narration: Which is from long ago: a quill or a phone? Tap the quill.
s06.social.lesson.06.steps.7.narration: Long ago and now — you can compare across time.
s06.social.lesson.06.title: Then and Now
s06.social.quiz.01.parentNote: Family stories beat any textbook here. Ask a grandparent what they used instead.
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.0.correctFe: Long ago, people used horses and carts.
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFeed: Which one is older? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.1.correctFe: A quill dipped in ink. Slow work!
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.1.prompt: People long ago wrote with a...
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.1.retryFeed: Phones are new. What came before? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.2.correctFe: People still write and travel. Only the how changed.
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.2.prompt: Tools change over time. What stays the same?
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.2.retryFeed: Do people still send messages today? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.3.correctFe: A fridge. Quills belong to then, not now.
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.3.prompt: Which would you find in a home today?
s06.social.quiz.01.questions.3.retryFeed: Which one is in your kitchen? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.01.title: Then vs. Now
s06.social.quiz.02.parentNote: Notice it out loud when they do it — 'you put that in the bin without being asked' teaches more than the quiz does.
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.0.prompt: Which is being a good citizen?
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.0.retryFeed: Which choice is kind to others? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.1.correctFe: Rules are how a group stays fair to everybody.
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.1.options.0: To keep everyone safe and fair
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.1.retryFeed: What would happen with no rules at all? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.2.correctFe: Helping without being asked counts most.
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.2.prompt: Someone drops their books in the hall. What do you do?
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.2.retryFeed: How would you want to be treated? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.3.correctFe: Small acts, done by many, change a whole place.
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.3.prompt: The park is full of litter. What helps most?
s06.social.quiz.02.questions.3.retryFeed: Which way gets it done faster? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.02.title: Good Citizen
s06.social.quiz.03.parentNote: Draw your own home from above together. Getting the view wrong once teaches it better than getting it right by luck.
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.0.correctFe: A map shows places from above.
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFeed: A map shows where things are. Try again!
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.1.prompt: A map shows things from which view?
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.1.retryFeed: Imagine standing on a chair. Try again!
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.2.correctFe: They turn a place into something you can read.
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.2.retryFeed: Why would a traveller carry one? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.3.correctFe: Looking down, a bed is a rectangle. Maps draw what you see.
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.3.options.0: That is its shape from above
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.3.prompt: On a room map, the bed looks like a small rectangle. Why?
s06.social.quiz.03.questions.3.retryFeed: Picture yourself on the ceiling. Try again!
s06.social.quiz.03.title: Find the Map
s06.social.quiz.04.parentNote: The test is simple: can you carry it home? Try it on the next shop you visit together.
s06.social.quiz.04.questions.0.correctFe: Bread is a good. You can hold it.
s06.social.quiz.04.questions.0.retryFeed: Which one can you carry home? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.04.questions.1.correctFe: A service. Work done for you, nothing to carry.
s06.social.quiz.04.questions.1.retryFeed: Which one is a job someone does? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.04.questions.2.correctFe: A service. Teaching is work, not a thing.
s06.social.quiz.04.questions.2.prompt: A teacher teaching a class is a...
s06.social.quiz.04.questions.2.retryFeed: Can you put a lesson in a bag? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.04.questions.3.correctFe: Both. You pay for a haircut and for bread alike.
s06.social.quiz.04.questions.3.retryFeed: Do you pay a doctor? Try again!
s06.social.quiz.04.title: Goods and Services
s06.social.story.01.pages.0.narration: The class park is full of litter. Nobody knows who dropped it.
s06.social.story.01.pages.1.narration: 'It is not our mess,' says one child. The others look at the ground.
s06.social.story.01.pages.2.narration: 'It is our park though,' says another. That settles it.
s06.social.story.01.pages.3.narration: Together they pick it all up. It takes less time than they feared.
s06.social.story.01.pages.4.narration: Then they plant a flower where the worst pile had been.
s06.social.story.01.pages.5.narration: Now the park is clean. Good citizens fix what is theirs to share.
s06.social.story.01.parentNote: Ask what they would do about a mess nobody made on purpose. That question is the whole lesson.
s06.social.story.01.title: Our Class Helps Out
s06.social.story.02.pages.0.narration: Juma is going to Grandma's house. Mum draws him a map.
s06.social.story.02.pages.1.narration: The map looks down on the street from above, like a bird.
s06.social.story.02.pages.2.narration: Past the school, then left at the big tree.
s06.social.story.02.pages.3.narration: At the tree, Juma stops. There are two paths, not one.
s06.social.story.02.pages.4.narration: He looks again. The map shows a river beside the right path.
s06.social.story.02.pages.5.narration: He hears the water and takes that path. Grandma is waiting.
s06.social.story.02.parentNote: Draw the route to somewhere real together afterwards. A map they made is one they can read.
s06.social.story.02.title: The Map to Grandma's
s06.tech.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: Which block moves the robot ahead?
s06.tech.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: What must you press to run your blocks?
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: The robot must reach the star. Drag a forward block.
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.1.feedback: Robot moves and reaches the star! 'You coded that!' ⭐
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.1.narration: Add turn left, then forward. Press play.
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.2.feedback: The robot follows your list exactly.
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.2.narration: The star moved. Drag forward, forward, turn right.
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.3.feedback: That is why order matters so much.
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.3.narration: Watch: a computer does what you wrote, not what you meant.
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.4.feedback: Fewer blocks, same star. Neat code!
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.4.narration: Two paths reach the star. Drag the shorter one.
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.5.feedback: Every block, in your order. You coded it!
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.5.narration: Press play and watch your program run.
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.6.narration: If the robot turns the wrong way, is the robot wrong or the code? Tap the code.
s06.tech.lesson.01.steps.7.narration: A program is a list of steps in order.
s06.tech.lesson.01.title: Guide the Robot
s06.tech.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: You sorted shapes that were red and…
s06.tech.lesson.02.recap.1.prompt: How many rules did you sort by?
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: Find the shapes that are red and round. Drag them to the box.
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: Two rules at once. Nice thinking!
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: Now find shapes that are blue and square. Drag them.
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: Watch: with two rules, a thing must pass both, not just one.
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.4.feedback: Two rules again. You are getting fast!
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.4.narration: Big and yellow. Drag only those.
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.5.feedback: No — red yes, round no. It must pass both.
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: A red square: does it pass 'red and round'? Tap no.
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.6.feedback: Sorting by rules is how computers find things!
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.6.narration: Sort your own toys by two rules and tap when done.
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.7.feedback: Computers sort by rules all day.
s06.tech.lesson.02.steps.7.narration: Two rules at once. That is logic.
s06.tech.lesson.02.title: Sort by Two Rules
s06.tech.lesson.03.recap.0.prompt: Steps in the right order make an…
s06.tech.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: When brushing teeth, what comes first?
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: Brushing teeth: wet brush, add paste, brush, rinse. Drag them in order.
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: Steps in order make an algorithm!
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: Making toast: get bread, toast it, spread it, eat. Drag them in order.
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.3.feedback: Order is part of the instruction.
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.3.narration: Watch: swap two steps and the whole thing breaks.
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.4.feedback: Socks first. Shoes will not fit otherwise!
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.4.narration: Getting dressed: socks before shoes. Drag them in order.
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.5.feedback: You debugged it. That is what coders do!
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.5.narration: Someone put 'rinse' before 'brush'. Tap the mistake.
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.6.narration: Do the same steps in a different order give the same result? Tap no.
s06.tech.lesson.03.steps.7.narration: Steps in the right order make an algorithm.
s06.tech.lesson.03.title: Steps in Order
s06.tech.lesson.04.recap.0.prompt: In the pattern red, red, ___, red, red, ___ what fills the gaps?
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: Red, red, blue, red, red, blue... tap what's next.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: Patterns repeat. What comes after that?
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: Circle, square, circle, square... tap what comes next.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.3.feedback: The repeat is the whole pattern.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.3.narration: Watch: find the part of the pattern that repeats, then say it again.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.4.feedback: Drum! Patterns work in sound too.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.4.narration: Listen: drum, drum, bell, drum, drum, bell... tap what comes next.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.5.feedback: You built a rule that keeps going!
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.5.narration: Make your own pattern with two colours and tap when done.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.6.feedback: Three long, then again. Well spotted.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.6.narration: In red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue — tap the part that repeats.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.7.feedback: Computers love patterns as much as you do.
s06.tech.lesson.04.steps.7.narration: Patterns repeat, and you can always find the repeat.
s06.tech.lesson.04.title: Spot the Pattern
s06.tech.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: Which part of a tablet do you see and tap?
s06.tech.lesson.05.recap.1.prompt: Which part turns it on and off?
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.0.feedback: The screen. It shows everything we tap.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: Which part do we look at and tap?
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.1.feedback: The button. It powers the tablet on and off.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: Which part turns the tablet on and off?
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: The tablet's speaker lets us hear. Tap the speaker.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.3.narration: Watch: each part has one job — show, hear, power, charge.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.4.feedback: A tiny eye on your tablet!
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.4.narration: The tablet's camera takes photos. Tap the camera.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.5.feedback: No charge, no tablet. That is its job.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.5.narration: The charger fills the battery. Tap the charger.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.6.feedback: The screen. The button only powers it.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.6.narration: The SCREEN shows the pictures; the button only powers the tablet. Tap the screen.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.7.feedback: Knowing the parts helps you ask for help.
s06.tech.lesson.05.steps.7.narration: You can name the parts of your tablet.
s06.tech.lesson.05.title: Parts of a Tablet
s06.tech.lesson.06.parentNote: Agree on a rule: always ask before sharing anything online.
s06.tech.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: If a screen asks for your name or photo, you should…
s06.tech.lesson.06.recap.1.prompt: Who helps keep you safe online?
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: If a screen asks for your name or a photo, stop. Tap to find a grown-up.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: Grown-ups help keep us safe online.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.1.prompt: Who helps keep you safe online?
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.2.feedback: Stop first, always. A grown-up decides.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: A game on the tablet asks for your photo. Tap to stop and ask.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.3.feedback: Private means yours, not the screen's.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.3.narration: Watch: your name, your photo and your home never go into a computer.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.4.feedback: Prizes on screens are usually tricks.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.4.narration: A window says you won a prize. Tap to close it and tell someone.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.5.feedback: You never have to answer a stranger.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.5.narration: Someone you do not know sends a message. Tap to tell a grown-up.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.6.feedback: No. That is private. Ask first.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.6.narration: Should you type your home address into the tablet? Tap no.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.7.feedback: That one habit keeps you safe online.
s06.tech.lesson.06.steps.7.narration: Stop, then ask a grown-up. Every time.
s06.tech.lesson.06.title: Stop and Ask
s06.tech.quiz.01.parentNote: Ask them to say the pattern out loud before choosing. Hearing the repeat is easier than seeing it.
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.0.correctFeed: You found the repeat. Circle comes next.
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.0.prompt: Circle, triangle, triangle, circle, triangle, triangle... next?
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFeedba: Look at the repeat. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.1.correctFeed: Three long, then it starts again.
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.1.prompt: In red, red, blue, red, red, blue — what repeats?
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.1.retryFeedba: Say it aloud until it loops. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.2.correctFeed: Clap. Patterns work in sound as well as sight.
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.2.prompt: Clap, stomp, clap, stomp... what comes next?
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.2.retryFeedba: Two things taking turns. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.3.correctFeed: Right. That is what a loop is for.
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.3.options.0.l: A repeat can be written once and reused
s06.tech.quiz.01.questions.3.retryFeedba: Would you rather write it once or ten times? Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.01.title: What Comes Next?
s06.tech.quiz.02.parentNote: Getting dressed and making toast are algorithms. Naming them that way at home costs nothing and sticks.
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.0.prompt: To brush teeth, what comes first?
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.0.retryFeedba: What do we do at the start? Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.1.correctFeed: Socks. Shoes will not fit over them otherwise!
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.1.retryFeedba: Picture putting socks on over shoes. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.2.correctFeed: A bug — a step in the wrong place. Fixing it is debugging.
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.2.prompt: Someone put 'rinse' before 'brush'. What is that called?
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.2.retryFeedba: It is the word coders use for a mistake. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.3.correctFeed: No. Order is part of the instruction.
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.3.prompt: Do the same steps in a different order give the same result?
s06.tech.quiz.02.questions.3.retryFeedba: Try shoes before socks and see. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.02.title: Steps in Order
s06.tech.quiz.03.parentNote: The habit that matters is stopping, not knowing which sites are safe. Praise the pause every time.
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.0.prompt: A screen asks for your name. What do you do?
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFeedba: Stay safe. Who should you ask? Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.1.correctFeed: Where you live is private. A colour is not.
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.1.retryFeedba: Which one could help a stranger find you? Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.2.correctFeed: A trick. Close it and tell a grown-up.
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.2.prompt: A pop-up says you won a prize. What is it probably?
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.2.retryFeedba: Do strangers really give away prizes? Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.3.correctFeed: Tell a grown-up. You never have to answer a stranger.
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.3.prompt: Someone you do not know sends you a message. What do you do?
s06.tech.quiz.03.questions.3.retryFeedba: Being polite does not mean replying. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.03.title: Online Safety
s06.tech.quiz.04.parentNote: 'And' means both, every time. Sorting laundry by 'dark and warm-wash' is the same skill.
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.0.correctFeed: The red ball passes both rules.
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.0.retryFeedba: It must be red AND round. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.1.correctFeed: No. Blue yes, round no — it must pass both.
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.1.prompt: Does a blue square pass 'blue and round'?
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.1.retryFeedba: One rule passed is not enough. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.2.correctFeed: 'And' is stricter. Fewer things get through.
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.2.prompt: Which is stricter: 'red and round' or 'red or round'?
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.2.retryFeedba: Which one lets more things through? Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.3.correctFeed: Sorting is how a computer finds one thing among millions.
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.3.prompt: Why do computers sort by rules?
s06.tech.quiz.04.questions.3.retryFeedba: Think of finding one book in a big library. Try again!
s06.tech.quiz.04.title: Sort by Two Rules
s06.tech.story.01.pages.0.narration: Robo's toys are all mixed up in one big heap.
s06.tech.story.01.pages.1.narration: 'One rule at a time,' says Robo. 'First, blocks with blocks.'
s06.tech.story.01.pages.2.narration: Then cars with cars. The heap gets smaller.
s06.tech.story.01.pages.3.narration: But the red blocks and the blue blocks are still muddled.
s06.tech.story.01.pages.4.narration: So Robo sorts again — by shape AND by colour. Two rules.
s06.tech.story.01.pages.5.narration: All tidy. 'Two rules found everything,' says Robo. 'Good logic!'
s06.tech.story.01.parentNote: Sorting by one rule is easy; by two is the real skill. Tidying up at home is the same puzzle.
s06.tech.story.01.title: Robo Sorts the Toys
s06.tech.story.02.pages.0.narration: Nia builds a robot. It does exactly what it is told. Exactly.
s06.tech.story.02.pages.1.narration: 'Put on your shoes, then your socks,' says Nia.
s06.tech.story.02.pages.2.narration: The robot puts the socks on over the shoes. Nia laughs.
s06.tech.story.02.pages.3.narration: 'You did what I said,' says Nia, 'not what I meant.'
s06.tech.story.02.pages.4.narration: She swaps the two steps around and runs the program again.
s06.tech.story.02.pages.5.narration: Socks, then shoes. Perfect. A program is only as good as its order.
s06.tech.story.02.parentNote: Try it for real: give an exact-steps instruction for making a sandwich and follow it literally. The laughing is the lesson.
s06.tech.story.02.title: The Robot That Took It Literally
s07.health.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: Which food group does an apple belong to?
s07.health.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: When should you wash your hands?
s07.health.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: Sort the apple into the fruits group.
s07.health.lesson.01.steps.1.feedback: Scrub-scrub for 20 seconds. 'All clean and healthy!'
s07.health.lesson.01.steps.1.narration: Tap to wash hands before eating.
s07.health.lesson.01.title: Food Groups and Hygiene
s07.health.lesson.02.parentNote: Wash hands together before meals and after the toilet.
s07.health.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: How long should you scrub your hands?
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.0.feedback: Clean-looking hands can still carry them.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: Germs are living things far too small to see. They can sit on your hands.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.1.feedback: Before eating. That is when hands go near your mouth.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: Germs get inside you through your mouth, so one moment matters most.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.1.prompt: When is it most important to wash?
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.2.feedback: The scrubbing is the part that works.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: Three steps: wet your hands, rub on soap, then scrub.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.3.feedback: Five slow counts. Keep going that long every time.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: Scrubbing takes longer than you think. Tap a bubble for each slow count.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.4.feedback: Germs hide in the places we rush past.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.4.narration: Do not forget between your fingers, and under your nails.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.5.feedback: Soap and water together. That is the pair that cleans.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: Water alone only pushes germs about. Soap lifts them off.
