s07.health.lesson.02.steps.6.feedback: Wash your hands. Before you touch food or your face.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.6.narration: You have been playing outside in the dirt. What now?
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.7.narration: Last step: dry with a clean cloth. Wet hands pick germs up again.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.8.feedback: Wet, soap, scrub, rinse, dry. Every time.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.8.narration: You know the whole routine now.
s07.health.lesson.02.steps.8.prompt: Which step actually removes the germs?
s07.health.lesson.02.title: Wash Your Hands
s07.health.lesson.03.parentNote: Build a colorful plate together at mealtime.
s07.health.lesson.03.recap.0.prompt: Which foods help us grow every day?
s07.health.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: Fruits and vegetables help us grow. Drag an apple to the plate.
s07.health.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: Sweets are 'sometimes' foods. Healthy foods are 'every day'.
s07.health.lesson.03.title: Healthy Foods
s07.health.lesson.04.recap.0.prompt: Running and jumping make our hearts…
s07.health.lesson.04.recap.1.prompt: How often should we move our bodies?
s07.health.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: Running and jumping make our hearts strong. Tap to jump!
s07.health.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: Moving every day keeps us healthy and happy.
s07.health.lesson.04.title: Move Your Body
s07.health.lesson.05.parentNote: Keep a calm, regular bedtime routine.
s07.health.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: What does sleep help our body and brain do?
s07.health.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: Sleep helps our body and brain rest and grow. Tap to dim the lights.
s07.health.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: A calm bedtime helps us sleep well.
s07.health.lesson.05.title: Good Sleep
s07.health.lesson.06.parentNote: Make helmets and seatbelts a no-exceptions habit.
s07.health.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: What should you wear to ride a bike?
s07.health.lesson.06.recap.1.prompt: What should you do in a car?
s07.health.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: Wear a helmet when you ride a bike. Tap to put it on.
s07.health.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: Buckle your seatbelt in the car. Tap to buckle.
s07.health.lesson.06.title: Safe and Sound
s07.health.quiz.01.questions.0.correctFe: Always tell a trusted grown-up. You are safe.
s07.health.quiz.01.questions.0.prompt: A stranger online asks for your home address. What do you do?
s07.health.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFeed: Never share private info online. Tell a grown-up. Try again!
s07.health.quiz.01.title: Safe or Unsafe?
s07.health.quiz.02.questions.0.correctFe: Before eating, and after the toilet.
s07.health.quiz.02.questions.0.prompt: When should you wash your hands?
s07.health.quiz.02.questions.0.retryFeed: Clean hands before food. Try again!
s07.health.quiz.02.title: When to Wash
s07.health.quiz.03.questions.0.correctFe: Apple slices are a healthy snack.
s07.health.quiz.03.questions.0.prompt: Which is a healthy everyday snack?
s07.health.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFeed: Which helps you grow? Try again!
s07.health.quiz.03.title: Healthy Snack
s07.health.story.01.pages.0.narration: Zoe wakes up, brushes her teeth, and eats fruit for breakfast.
s07.health.story.01.pages.1.narration: She runs and plays outside, then washes her hands for lunch.
s07.health.story.01.pages.2.narration: After a calm bedtime, she sleeps well. A healthy day!
s07.health.story.01.parentNote: Talk through your child's own healthy-day habits.
s07.health.story.01.title: A Healthy Day with Zoe
s07.math.lesson.01.title: Add and Subtract Within 20
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: Big sums can be easy. Watch this one: 8 + 7.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.1.feedback: So let's make a ten first.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: Ten is our friend. It is easy to add to ten.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: Eight is nearly ten. How much more does it need? 8 + ? = 10.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.3.feedback: Let's see how much is left.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: We borrowed that 2 from the 7. Now take it away: 7 - 2.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: Now the hard sum has become an easy one: 10 + 5.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.6.narration: So 8 + 7 = 15. Making ten turned a hard sum into an easy one.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.7.narration: Your turn. We want to add 9 + 6.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.7.prompt: What does 9 need to make ten?
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.8.feedback: 10 and 5 is 15. You did it the clever way!
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.8.narration: Take 1 from the 6 to make ten, then add what is left.
s07.math.lesson.02.steps.9.feedback: 12! Making ten works every single time.
s07.math.lesson.02.title: Add to 20
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: Taking away can use the same ten trick. Try 15 − 7.
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.1.feedback: Ten is an easy place to stand.
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: Instead of taking all 7 at once, we step down to ten first.
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.3.narration: We have taken 5 of the 7 away. Two more still to go.
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.4.narration: Take the last 2 from our ten.
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.5.narration: Down to ten, then down again. That is the whole trick.
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.6.narration: This one lands on ten in a single step.
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.7.feedback: 9! Four to reach ten, then one more.
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.7.narration: 14 − 5. Step down to ten, then take what is left.
s07.math.lesson.03.steps.8.feedback: 9! You are subtracting like a mathematician.
s07.math.lesson.03.title: Subtract to 20
s07.math.lesson.04.recap.0.prompt: In the number 47, how many tens?
s07.math.lesson.04.recap.1.prompt: In the number 47, how many ones?
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: Big numbers are made of tens and ones. Look at 47.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.1.feedback: Where a digit stands changes what it is worth.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: The 4 is not really four. It means four bundles of ten: 40.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: Count the bundles of ten in 47.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.3.narration: The loose ones are the leftovers that could not make a bundle.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.4.feedback: Every two-digit number works this way.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.4.narration: Say it out loud: forty… seven. The number tells you its own parts.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.5.narration: Now backwards: build the number from its parts.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.5.prompt: Which number has 6 tens and 2 ones?
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.6.feedback: 80. A zero holds the ones place open.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.6.narration: Careful with this one. There are no loose ones at all.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.7.narration: Tens are worth more than ones, so look at the tens first.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.8.feedback: 59! You can read any number now.
s07.math.lesson.04.steps.8.narration: Last one: build 5 tens and 9 ones.
s07.math.lesson.04.title: Tens and Ones to 99
s07.math.lesson.05.parentNote: Point out o'clock times on a real clock together.
s07.math.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: The big hand pointing to 12 means…
s07.math.lesson.05.recap.1.prompt: Little hand on 3, big hand on 12. What time is it?
s07.math.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: The big hand is on 12, the little hand on 3. That's 3 o'clock. Tap 3 o'clock.
s07.math.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: When the big hand points up to 12, we say 'o'clock'.
s07.math.lesson.05.title: Tell Time to the Hour
s07.math.lesson.06.parentNote: Sort and count coins together (use your local currency).
s07.math.lesson.06.recap.1.prompt: What is one of those coins worth on its own?
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.0.feedback: Size does not tell you the value. The number does.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: Coins are small, but each one is worth a different amount.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.1.feedback: 10 is worth more than 5, even if the coin looks smaller.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: Read the number on each coin.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.1.prompt: Which is worth more, a 5 or a 10?
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.2.feedback: Three coins, but we still do not know how much money that is.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: Tap each coin in the pile to count them.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.3.feedback: To find the money, add the values.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.3.narration: Counting coins is not the same as counting money.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.5.feedback: 16. Add the big ones first. It is easier.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.5.narration: Now a 10, a 5 and a 1 together.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.6.feedback: 20 is more than 15, so you can buy it.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.6.prompt: Do you have enough to buy the mango?
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.7.feedback: 5 back. Now you know how to check your change.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.7.narration: The seller gives back what is left over. That is your change.
s07.math.lesson.06.steps.8.narration: Sometimes different coins make the same amount.
s07.math.lesson.06.title: Coins and Money
s07.math.quiz.01.questions.0.correctFeed: You read the graph. Apples have the tallest bar.
s07.math.quiz.01.questions.0.prompt: Which fruit got the most votes on the graph?
s07.math.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFeedba: Find the tallest bar. Try again!
s07.math.quiz.01.title: Read the Bar Graph
s07.math.quiz.02.questions.0.retryFeedba: Make ten first: 8 + 2, then 5. Try again!
s07.math.quiz.02.title: Add Within 20
s07.math.quiz.03.questions.0.prompt: The little hand is on 6, big hand on 12. What time is it?
s07.math.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFeedba: The little hand shows the hour. Try again!
s07.math.quiz.03.title: What Time?
s07.math.story.01.pages.0.narration: Lila saves coins in a jar for a kite.
s07.math.story.01.pages.1.narration: She has two 5-coins. Tap to count: 5, 10!
s07.math.story.01.pages.2.narration: Ten is enough for the kite! Off she runs to buy it.
s07.math.story.01.title: The Coin Jar
s07.reading.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: Add silent-e to cap. What word do you get?
s07.reading.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: Which sound do the letters a and i make in rain?
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.0.feedback: Short and quick. The a says /a/.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.1.feedback: The word changed, and so did the middle sound.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.1.narration: Now watch. We add one letter at the end: cape.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.2.feedback: cape. The e is there but stays quiet.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.2.narration: Read it again: cape. The new e is silent. You never say it out loud.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.3.feedback: cap becomes cape. hop becomes hope.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.3.narration: Here is the magic: silent e makes the vowel read its own name. A says 'ay'.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.4.feedback: hope has it. hop and hopping do not.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.4.narration: Look for the quiet e at the end of the word.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.4.prompt: Which word has a silent e?
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.5.feedback: That is called a vowel team.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.5.narration: There is a second way vowels help each other. Two vowels together, one sound: rain.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.6.narration: Find the two letters doing the work in rain.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.7.narration: Listen for that same /ay/ sound in another word.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.7.prompt: Which word has the same sound as rain?
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.8.feedback: Four new words from one pattern.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.8.narration: Once you spot a team you can read a whole family: rain, pain, mail, tail.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.9.feedback: tail. A and i again. You are reading with patterns now.
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.9.narration: Read this sentence: 'The tail is long.'
s07.reading.lesson.01.steps.9.prompt: Which word has a vowel team?
s07.reading.lesson.01.title: Silent-e and Vowel Teams
s07.reading.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: Which word has the short a sound?
s07.reading.lesson.02.recap.1.prompt: What does silent-e do to the vowel?
s07.reading.lesson.02.steps.1.feedback: '/ay/. Long a, cape! The e makes a say its name.'
s07.reading.lesson.02.title: Short and Long Vowels
s07.reading.lesson.03.recap.0.prompt: How many sounds does the blend bl make?
s07.reading.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: Which blend begins the word star: st or bl?
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.0.feedback: /b/ and /l/, close together but both there.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: Sometimes two letters stand side by side and you hear both. Listen: bl in black.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: Say black slowly and listen to the very start.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.2.feedback: 2 sounds. You can hear them both if you go slowly.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: A blend is two sounds, not one new sound.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.2.prompt: How many sounds do you hear in 'bl'?
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.3.feedback: Learn one blend, unlock many words.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.3.narration: Blends come in families too: st in stop, star, stand.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.4.narration: Which of these begins with that st sound?
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.5.feedback: nd. Both sounds, right at the finish.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.5.narration: Blends can hide at the end of a word too. Listen to the end of hand: /n/ /d/.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.6.narration: Say each one and listen to the last part.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.7.narration: Here is a new word to sound out: frog.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.7.prompt: Which blend do you see in 'frog'?
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.8.feedback: That is what blends are for.
s07.reading.lesson.03.steps.8.narration: bl, st, nd, fr. You can now sound out words you have never seen before.
s07.reading.lesson.03.title: Consonant Blends
s07.reading.lesson.04.recap.0.prompt: 'The girl kicks the ball.' Who does the kicking?
s07.reading.lesson.04.recap.1.prompt: In that sentence, what gets kicked?
s07.reading.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: Read: 'The girl kicks the ball.' Who kicks? Tap the girl.
s07.reading.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: What does she kick? Tap the ball.
s07.reading.lesson.04.title: Read for Meaning
s07.reading.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: A retelling goes beginning, middle, and…
s07.reading.lesson.05.recap.1.prompt: Retelling a story shows that you…
s07.reading.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: Put the story parts in order: beginning, middle, end.
s07.reading.lesson.05.title: Retell the Story
s07.reading.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: A text tells how an animal eats, plays and sleeps. The main idea is…
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.0.feedback: One sentence so far. Keep listening.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: Listen to this little story. 'Bees live together in a hive.'
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.1.feedback: Three more sentences. Notice what they are all about.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: 'Some bees find flowers. Some bees make honey. Some keep the hive clean.'
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.2.feedback: Honey. That is a detail. One fact from one sentence.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: Before we think about the whole story, check one thing you heard.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.3.feedback: It is mostly about bees working together.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.3.narration: Now the whole story. Every sentence talked about bees doing a job.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.3.prompt: What is this story mostly about?
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.4.feedback: It is the whole story in a few words.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.4.narration: That is the main idea: what most of the sentences are about.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.5.feedback: 'Some bees make honey' is one small detail, not the whole idea.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.5.narration: The other sentences are details. They fill in the picture.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.5.prompt: Which one is a detail, not the main idea?
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.6.feedback: Titles are a clue to what a story is about.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.6.narration: A good title is the main idea, made short.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.7.feedback: 'Busy Bees'. Short, and it says the main idea.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.7.narration: Pick the title that fits our bee story.
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.8.feedback: Ask yourself: what are all three about?
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.8.narration: Now a brand new story. 'Rain fills the river. Plants drink. Animals come to the water.'
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.9.feedback: Rain helps life grow. You found a main idea on your own!
s07.reading.lesson.06.steps.9.narration: Find the idea that holds all three sentences together.
s07.reading.lesson.06.title: Main Idea
s07.reading.quiz.01.questions.0.prompt: Dark clouds roll in and the wind blows. What will probably happen?
s07.reading.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFee: What do dark clouds bring? Try again!
s07.reading.quiz.01.title: Predict What Happens
s07.reading.quiz.02.questions.0.correctF: Long i. The e makes the i say its name.
s07.reading.quiz.02.questions.0.prompt: Does 'kite' have a long or short vowel?
s07.reading.quiz.02.title: Long or Short?
s07.reading.quiz.03.questions.0.correctF: The whole story is about how plants grow.
s07.reading.quiz.03.questions.0.prompt: A story tells how a seed grows into a plant. It is mostly about...
s07.reading.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFee: What was the whole story about? Try again!
s07.reading.quiz.03.title: What Was It About?
s07.reading.story.01.pages.0.narration: A small puppy could not find its way home. (Tap a word to hear it.)
s07.reading.story.01.pages.1.narration: A kind girl saw it and read its name tag.
s07.reading.story.01.pages.2.narration: She walked it home. The puppy wagged its tail. The end!
s07.reading.story.01.parentNote: Ask: what happened first, next, and last?
s07.reading.story.01.title: The Lost Puppy
s07.science.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: Which comes first in a butterfly's life?
s07.science.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: After the caterpillar and chrysalis comes a…
s07.science.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: Put them in order. What comes first?
s07.science.lesson.01.steps.1.feedback: A butterfly! egg → caterpillar → chrysalis → butterfly.
s07.science.lesson.01.title: Life Cycle of a Butterfly
s07.science.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: Which stage comes right after the egg?
s07.science.lesson.02.recap.1.prompt: A cycle that repeats over and over is called a…
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: A butterfly does not start as a butterfly. It starts as a tiny egg on a leaf.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: Out of the egg comes a caterpillar. It eats and eats and grows.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.2.feedback: Caterpillar comes right after the egg.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: Put the first two stages in order in your head.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.2.prompt: What comes right after the egg?
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.3.feedback: From outside, nothing seems to happen.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.3.narration: Then the caterpillar makes a hard case around itself. That case is a chrysalis.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.4.feedback: It is changing its whole body.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.4.narration: Inside the chrysalis it is very busy indeed.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.4.prompt: What is happening inside the chrysalis?
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.5.feedback: The same animal. A completely new shape.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.5.narration: The case opens and a butterfly climbs out with new wings.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.6.narration: Now you put all four in order: egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.7.feedback: 4 stages, always in the same order.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.8.feedback: A cycle. It goes round and round forever.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.8.narration: Then the butterfly lays eggs, and it all begins again.
s07.science.lesson.02.steps.8.prompt: What do we call something that repeats like this?
s07.science.lesson.02.title: A Butterfly's Life Cycle
s07.science.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: Which body part helps us breathe?

s10.reading.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: 'It's raining cats and dogs' doesn't mean animals fall! It means raining hard. Tap the real meaning.
s10.reading.lesson.02.steps.1.feedback: Right, not a real wish to get hurt.
s10.reading.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: 'Break a leg' means 'good luck'. Tap the kind meaning.
s10.reading.lesson.02.steps.2.feedback: Something very easy. Idioms are fun once you learn them.

s10.reading.lesson.03.steps.0.feedback: Theme = the message behind the story.
s10.reading.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: A theme is the big lesson, like 'never give up' or 'kindness matters'. It's not just what happens.
s10.reading.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: In a tale where a slow tortoise wins by trying hard, the theme is...?
s10.reading.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: Ask: what did the character learn? That points to the theme.
s10.reading.lesson.03.title: Finding the Theme

s10.reading.lesson.04.recap.1.prompt: 'She ran home' is told in which point of view?

s10.reading.lesson.04.steps.1.feedback: Right. 'She ran home' is third person.
s10.reading.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: Third person uses 'he', 'she', 'they'. A narrator outside the story. Tap it.
s10.reading.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: Who is telling the story changes how we see it.
s10.reading.lesson.04.steps.2.prompt: What changes how we see it?

s10.reading.lesson.05.steps.0.feedback: A summary is short and focused.
s10.reading.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: A summary keeps only the most important ideas. Who, what, and why. Skip tiny details.
s10.reading.lesson.05.steps.1.feedback: The color of the collar isn't a key point.
s10.reading.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: Read a paragraph about a rescue dog. Tap the sentence that is just a small detail.
s10.reading.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: Now keep the main events in order to build your summary.

s10.reading.lesson.06.steps.1.feedback: You combined clues with what you know.

s10.science.lesson.01.steps.1.feedback: The light goes out. A broken circuit stops the flow.

s10.science.story.01.pages.0.narration: Every night, Nadia drew the Moon from her window. Some nights it was a thin sliver; other nights, a full bright circle.
s10.science.story.01.pages.1.narration: Her drawings showed a pattern: the Moon seemed to grow, then shrink, over about a month. Tap to see her moon journal.
s10.science.story.01.pages.2.narration: Grandpa smiled. 'The Moon isn't changing shape. Sunlight just lights up different parts as it orbits Earth.' Nadia grinned: science was everywhere!
s10.science.story.01.title: Nadia and the Night Sky
s10.social.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: Which lines run side to side across a map?
s10.social.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: What is the line around the middle of Earth called?
s10.social.lesson.01.steps.0.feedback: 'The equator circles the middle of Earth.'
s10.social.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: Latitude lines run side to side. Tap the equator (0 degrees).
s10.social.lesson.01.steps.1.feedback: 'Together they give every place an address.'
s10.social.lesson.01.steps.1.narration: Longitude lines run top to bottom. Tap one.
s10.social.lesson.01.title: Latitude and Longitude
s10.social.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: Which branch carries out the laws?
s10.social.lesson.02.recap.1.prompt: Which branch decides what laws mean?
s10.social.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: The legislative branch makes laws. Drag the lawmakers to 'makes laws'.
s10.social.lesson.02.steps.1.feedback: The executive puts laws into action.
s10.social.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: The executive branch carries out laws, led by a president or prime minister. Drag it to 'carries out'.
s10.social.lesson.02.steps.2.feedback: Three branches share power and balance each other.
s10.social.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: The judicial branch decides what laws mean. Courts and judges. Drag it to 'interprets'.
s10.social.lesson.02.title: Three Branches of Government
s10.social.lesson.03.recap.0.prompt: When many people want a scarce item, the price often…
s10.social.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: A haircut is helpful work, so it is a…
s10.social.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: A good is something you can hold, like bread. A service is helpful work, like a haircut. Tap the service.
s10.social.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: When many people want a scarce item, demand is high and the price often rises.
s10.social.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: People trade goods and services to get what they need.
s10.social.lesson.03.title: Goods, Services, and Trade
s10.social.lesson.04.recap.0.prompt: How many continents does Earth have?
s10.social.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: Earth has seven continents. Tap Africa, the second-largest.
s10.social.lesson.04.steps.1.feedback: The Pacific is the biggest ocean.
s10.social.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: Five oceans cover most of Earth. Tap the Pacific, the largest.
s10.social.lesson.04.steps.2.feedback: Now you can find places worldwide.
s10.social.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: Maps use a compass and a key to help us read them.
s10.social.lesson.04.steps.2.prompt: What helps us read a map?
s10.social.lesson.04.title: Continents and Oceans
s10.social.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: The Empire of Mali grew rich trading gold and…
s10.social.lesson.05.recap.1.prompt: Which city became a famous centre of learning?
s10.social.lesson.05.steps.0.feedback: Caravans crossed the Sahara to trade.
s10.social.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: Long ago, the Empire of Mali grew rich from trading gold and salt. Tap the trade routes.
s10.social.lesson.05.steps.1.feedback: Scholars came from far away to study.
s10.social.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: The city of Timbuktu became a famous center of learning and books. Tap Timbuktu.
s10.social.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: Leaders like Mansa Musa were known across the world. History is full of great civilizations.
s10.social.lesson.05.steps.2.prompt: Who led the Empire of Mali?
s10.social.lesson.05.title: The Empire of Mali
s10.social.lesson.06.parentNote: Talk about one way your family helps the community.
s10.social.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: How do citizens help choose their leaders?
s10.social.lesson.06.recap.1.prompt: Following fair rules and helping others are citizens'…
s10.social.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: Citizens have rights, like learning and speaking freely. Tap a right.
s10.social.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: Citizens also have responsibilities, like following fair rules and helping others. Tap a responsibility.
s10.social.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: Voting is how citizens help choose leaders and decisions.
s10.social.lesson.06.title: Being a Good Citizen
s10.social.quiz.01.questions.0.correctFe: A castle. Thick stone walls kept people safe.

s10.social.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFeed: Think tall stone walls and a moat. Try again!
s10.social.quiz.01.title: Medieval Life

s10.social.quiz.02.title: Which Branch?

s10.social.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFeed: It borders Asia and the Americas. Try again!
s10.social.quiz.03.questions.1.correctFe: A haircut is a service, which is helpful work.
s10.social.quiz.03.questions.1.prompt: A haircut is an example of a...
s10.social.quiz.03.questions.1.retryFeed: Can you hold it in your hand? If not, it's a service. Try again!
s10.social.quiz.03.title: World and Work
s10.social.story.01.pages.0.narration: Greenfield town had one big question: should the empty lot become a park or a parking area? People disagreed.
s10.social.story.01.pages.1.narration: At the town meeting, everyone listened to both sides. Then citizens voted. One person, one vote. Tap to cast a vote.
s10.social.story.01.pages.2.narration: The park won by a small margin. Some were disappointed, but all agreed the choice was fair. That's how democracy works!
s10.social.story.01.title: The Town Vote
s10.writing.lesson.01.recap.0.prompt: Which part of an essay comes first?
s10.writing.lesson.01.recap.1.prompt: Which part gives the reasons and details?
s10.writing.lesson.01.steps.0.narration: The introduction tells the main idea and grabs attention. Drag it to the top.
s10.writing.lesson.01.steps.1.narration: The body paragraphs give reasons and details. Drag them to the middle.
s10.writing.lesson.01.steps.2.feedback: Intro, body, conclusion. A strong essay.
s10.writing.lesson.01.steps.2.narration: The conclusion wraps up and restates the big idea. Drag it to the end.
s10.writing.lesson.01.title: Parts of an Essay
s10.writing.lesson.02.recap.0.prompt: What does a topic sentence do?
s10.writing.lesson.02.steps.0.feedback: It tells the reader the big idea.
s10.writing.lesson.02.steps.0.narration: A topic sentence states the paragraph's main idea: 'Dogs make great pets.' Tap the topic sentence.
s10.writing.lesson.02.steps.1.narration: Supporting details give reasons: 'They are loyal. They help us exercise.' Tap a supporting detail.
s10.writing.lesson.02.steps.2.narration: Strong paragraphs are one clear idea plus reasons that fit it.
s10.writing.lesson.02.title: Topic Sentence and Support
s10.writing.lesson.03.recap.1.prompt: Which word shows cause and effect?
s10.writing.lesson.03.steps.0.narration: Transitions like 'first', 'next', and 'finally' show order. Tap the order word.
s10.writing.lesson.03.steps.1.narration: 'However' and 'but' show a change or contrast. Tap the contrast word.
s10.writing.lesson.03.steps.2.narration: 'Because' and 'so' show cause and effect. Good writing flows with links.
s10.writing.lesson.03.title: Linking Words
s10.writing.lesson.04.recap.0.prompt: What goes around the exact words spoken?
s10.writing.lesson.04.recap.1.prompt: When do you start a new line in dialogue?
s10.writing.lesson.04.steps.0.narration: Put quotation marks around the exact words spoken: "Let's go," said Maria. Tap the quotation marks.
s10.writing.lesson.04.steps.1.narration: A comma goes inside before the closing quote when a tag follows. Tap the comma.
s10.writing.lesson.04.steps.2.feedback: Now your dialogue is clear and correct.
s10.writing.lesson.04.steps.2.narration: Start a new line each time a new person speaks.
s10.writing.lesson.04.steps.2.prompt: When does a new line start?
s10.writing.lesson.04.title: Punctuating Dialogue
s10.writing.lesson.05.recap.0.prompt: Writing that tells a story is…
s10.writing.lesson.05.recap.1.prompt: Writing that tries to convince you is…
s10.writing.lesson.05.steps.0.feedback: Narrative is a tale with events.
s10.writing.lesson.05.steps.0.narration: Narrative writing tells a story. Tap the story example.
s10.writing.lesson.05.steps.1.narration: Informative writing explains facts. Tap the explaining example.
s10.writing.lesson.05.steps.2.narration: Persuasive writing tries to convince you. Tap the convincing example.
s10.writing.lesson.05.title: Three Kinds of Writing
s10.writing.lesson.06.parentNote: Ask your child to read a draft aloud — it helps them catch what to improve.
s10.writing.lesson.06.recap.0.prompt: Which comes first when improving a draft?
s10.writing.lesson.06.recap.1.prompt: Fixing spelling, capitals and punctuation is…
s10.writing.lesson.06.steps.0.narration: Revising improves ideas: add a detail or a clearer word. Tap the sentence that needs more detail.
s10.writing.lesson.06.steps.1.narration: Editing fixes spelling, capitals, and punctuation. Tap the editing mistake.
s10.writing.lesson.06.steps.2.feedback: Revise, then edit. That's the secret.
s10.writing.lesson.06.steps.2.narration: Great writers reread and improve their work.
s10.writing.lesson.06.title: Revise and Edit
s10.writing.quiz.01.questions.0.correctF: It argues an opinion and urges action.
Everyone should recycle because it protects our future.
Recycling turns old materials into new products.
s10.writing.quiz.01.questions.0.prompt: Which sentence is persuasive (tries to convince you)?
s10.writing.quiz.01.questions.0.retryFee: Which one tells you what you should do? Try again!
Water boils at 100°C at sea level.
Science is the most exciting subject.
s10.writing.quiz.01.questions.1.prompt: Which is a fact, not an opinion?
s10.writing.quiz.01.questions.1.retryFee: An opinion is a feeling; a fact can be checked. Try again!
s10.writing.quiz.01.title: Spot the Persuasive Sentence
s10.writing.quiz.02.questions.0.correctF: It states the main idea. The others are details.
Recess is the best part of school.
s10.writing.quiz.02.questions.0.prompt: Which is the topic sentence? 'Recess is the best part of school. We play games. We get fresh air.'
s10.writing.quiz.02.questions.0.retryFee: The topic sentence states the big idea. Try again!
s10.writing.quiz.02.title: Find the Topic Sentence
s10.writing.quiz.03.questions.0.prompt: 'I wanted to play outside. ___, it was raining.' Which word fits?
s10.writing.quiz.03.questions.0.retryFee: The sentence shows a change of plan. Try again!
s10.writing.quiz.03.questions.1.retryFee: Which word tells when something happens? Try again!
s10.writing.quiz.03.title: Pick the Transition
s10.writing.story.01.pages.0.narration: Jamal was chosen to give a speech about why the school needs a garden. He stared at a blank page, unsure how to start.
s10.writing.story.01.pages.1.narration: He made a plan: an introduction, three reasons, and a strong ending. Then he wrote a messy first draft. Tap to help him add a transition word.
s10.writing.story.01.pages.2.narration: Jamal revised, edited, and practiced aloud. On the big day, his clear, organized speech won applause, and a new school garden!
s10.writing.story.01.title: Jamal's Big Speech
